findings.title: Uncapped per-day liquidated damages calculated on total fees
findings.deviation: Section 11.2 imposes liquidated damages of 2% of the Total Fees per calendar day, which is uncapped and calculated on the total contract value rather than the milestone value, and Section 11.3 makes these damages cumulative with actual damages.
findings.impact: This creates severe, unlimited financial exposure for the performing party, which does not meet AtliQ's commercial standards.
findings.quote: If Vendor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Vendor shall pay AtliQ, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Fees for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week of delay attributable to the performing party, capped at 5% of that milestone fee, as the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

findings.title: Conditional pay-when-paid term with excessive payment window
findings.deviation: Section 4.3 conditions payment to the vendor on AtliQ receiving payment from the End Client and allows up to 120 days for payment.
findings.impact: This creates unpredictable payment timelines and delays payment to the performing party far beyond AtliQ's 45-day maximum standard.
findings.quote: AtliQ's obligation to pay any invoice is conditional upon AtliQ's receipt of payment from the End Client for the corresponding services. AtliQ shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) days after AtliQ receives the corresponding payment from the End Client, and in any event not later than one hundred and twenty (120) days after AtliQ's receipt of the invoice.
findings.counterPosition: Payment within 30 days of receipt of invoice (45 days maximum) with no pay-when-paid condition.

findings.title: One-way uncapped liability structure for vendor
findings.deviation: Section 10.3 completely excludes the vendor from any liability cap, while Section 10.2 caps AtliQ's liability at fees paid.
findings.impact: This leaves the performing party with unlimited liability exposure under the contract.
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE VENDOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING VENDOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.
findings.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1x fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim, with standard carve-outs for fraud, wilful misconduct, and confidentiality.

findings.title: One-way indemnity covering AtliQ's own negligence
findings.deviation: Section 9.1 requires the vendor to indemnify AtliQ for any and all losses, including those caused in whole or in part by AtliQ's own negligence, and is one-sided and uncapped.
findings.impact: This forces the performing party to cover losses arising from the other party's own negligent acts.
findings.quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless AtliQ, its Affiliates, and their respective directors, officers, employees, agents, successors and assigns (the "AtliQ Indemnitees") from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) the Services or Deliverables, (b) any breach of this Agreement by Vendor, (c) any claim by the End Client relating to the Services or Deliverables, or (d) any act or omission of Vendor Personnel, in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any AtliQ Indemnitee.
findings.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own non-performance or negligence, with no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence.

findings.title: Short notice convenience termination without payment for work in progress
findings.deviation: Section 5.3 allows AtliQ to terminate on only 7 days' notice without obligation to pay for work in progress or unaccepted deliverables.
findings.impact: This deprives the performing party of fair compensation for services already performed prior to termination.
findings.quote: AtliQ may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Vendor. Upon such termination, AtliQ's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by AtliQ prior to the effective date of termination; AtliQ shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
findings.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to the date of termination, including work in progress, with a mutual notice period of at least 30 days.

findings.title: Vendor retains ownership of deliverables under a non-exclusive license
findings.deviation: Section 7.2 and 7.3 allow the vendor to retain ownership of specifically created annotation outputs and deliverables while granting AtliQ only a non-exclusive, non-transferable license, but the client contract requires exclusive and transferable rights to specifically created Work Results.
findings.impact: AtliQ will be unable to transfer the exclusive rights promised to the client, resulting in non-compliance with the client contract.
findings.quote: Vendor shall retain all right, title and interest in and to its tools, labelling platform, scripts, ontologies, annotation guidelines developed by Vendor, and annotation outputs, including all intellectual property rights therein (collectively, "Vendor IP"). ... Subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Vendor grants AtliQ a non-exclusive, non-transferable, perpetual licence to use the annotation outputs and Deliverables for the purposes of the End Client project, including delivery to the End Client.
findings.counterPosition: Ensure all rights, title, and interest in specifically created deliverables and annotation outputs are assigned to AtliQ upon creation or payment, with pre-existing vendor materials licensed broadly enough to meet client requirements.
findings.linkedQuote: Except for PipeKit, Client shall acquire the exclusive, perpetual, transferable and unrestricted right of use in all Work Results created specifically for Client, upon full payment of the relevant Milestone Fee.

findings.title: Missing data processing agreement and personnel training flowdowns
findings.deviation: The subcontractor agreement fails to include a Data Processing Agreement or requirements for data protection training, despite the fact that the subcontractor will access and process personal data (technician names) and the client contract explicitly mandates a DPA and trained personnel.
findings.impact: AtliQ will be in non-compliance with its GDPR obligations under the client contract to ensure subcontractors are bound to a DPA and properly trained.
findings.quote: Source data comprises vibration, temperature and pressure sensor streams from End Client customer plants, together with maintenance work orders and technician logs (including technician names, shift identifiers and free-text notes). Vendor Personnel shall access data via AtliQ-provisioned cloud workspaces and Vendor's own labelling platform.
findings.counterPosition: Execute a back-to-back Data Processing Agreement (DPA) incorporating EU Standard Contractual Clauses, and require the vendor to ensure all personnel receive appropriate data protection training and are bound by confidentiality.
findings.linkedQuote: To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Client, the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR attached as Annex 3... Supplier shall ensure that its personnel are bound to confidentiality and data secrecy and receive appropriate data protection training.

findings.title: Missing requirement to obtain client's prior consent for subcontracting
findings.deviation: The subcontractor agreement does not condition the engagement or the start date on obtaining the required prior written consent from the client, even though the client contract explicitly mandates such consent.
findings.impact: AtliQ would be in non-compliance with its client commitments by engaging the subcontractor without securing prior written consent.
findings.quote: Vendor shall not subcontract any portion of the Services without AtliQ's prior written consent.
findings.counterPosition: Add a condition precedent stating that the agreement is contingent upon AtliQ obtaining prior written consent from the End Client.
findings.linkedQuote: Supplier may subcontract parts of the services only with Client's prior written consent.

findings.title: Subcontractor start scheduled prior to client contract execution
findings.deviation: The subcontractor is scheduled to start performance on October 5, 2026, which is before the client contract is finalized and executed.
findings.impact: AtliQ risks incurring costs and liabilities to the subcontractor without a signed revenue-generating agreement with the client.
findings.counterPosition: Align the subcontractor's start date to be contingent upon the full execution of the client contract.
findings.linkedQuote: This Agreement enters into force upon signature by both Parties and ends upon acceptance of the final Milestone and expiry of the warranty period.

fine.note: No restrictive covenants or non-competes are imposed on the vendor.
Confidentiality obligations protect AtliQ and the End Client appropriately for a subcontract.
Representations and warranties are standard and appropriate.
